stem_book: For the reaction 2M + N → product, a chemist mixes 6 mol of M with 4 mol of N, then adds 2 mol more of N (M remains 6 mol). What happens to the amount of product formed? (a) Product increases because N was limiting and now is excess (b) Product remains unchanged because M is the limiting reagent (c) Product doubles because N increases (d) Product becomes zero because M is now excess
key: b Product remains unchanged because M is the limiting reagent
derived: b Product remains unchanged because M is the limiting reagent
correct_answer: b Product remains unchanged because M is the limiting reagent
work: 6 mol M needs 3 mol N < 4 mol present ⇒ M limiting before and after adding N ⇒ product = 3 mol, unchanged
